title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 46–47 of Grothendieck's own numbering). He is studying the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, meaning the boundary strata of the stable compactification and their neighbourhoods. A stratum is indexed by a 'ν-graph', the dual graph of a stable curve. Here a ν-graph is G = (S, Ã, σ_Ã, o_G; I → S; g: S → N) in half-edge form:
- S is the set of vertices (components);
- Ã is the set of half-edges, with σ_Ã a fixed-point-free involution (edges = orbits) and o: Ã → S the origin map;
- I → S places the marked points (legs) on components;
- g: S → N gives the genera.

The previous page describes a 'localisation' construction. One takes a subgraph G' ⊂ G (vertex set S' ⊂ S, half-edge set Ã' stable under σ and mapped into S'). The cut half-edges are J̃ = Ã \ Ã'. One then chooses a set of legs I' ⊂ I ⊔ J̃ lying over S'. The most important case is the point subgraph {α}, with I' = I_α ⊔ Ã_α. Geometrically, the part of a degenerate curve lying over G' is itself a degenerate pointed curve whose marked points are the old markings plus the nodes cut open.

This page axiomatises that as a category. A 'morphisme de localisation' G' → G is a pair (f_G, f_I) such that:
(a) f_G: G' → G is a graph homomorphism, injective on vertices and on edges, so it identifies G' with a subgraph of G.
(b) f_I: I' → I ⊔ Ã is injective, with image in I ⊔ J̃, where J̃ = Ã − f_G(Ã'). The square (129) commutes: I' → I ⊔ Ã over S' → S, via the origin maps.
(c) (margin) Genera are preserved: g'(s') = g(f_G(s')).

The morphism is called 'strict' when the legs of G' are exactly the full fibre of I ⊔ J̃ over S'. Non-strict morphisms also allow some legs to be dropped, which amounts to building forgetful maps into the morphism.

ν-graphs with these morphisms form a category under composition. The page then starts to relate this notion to an 'orthodox' notion of graph morphism 'in the same direction'. Page 47 continues by introducing 'graphs with open branches', i.e. 1-complexes with a finite vertex set and non-compact open edges.

In modern terms these are subgraph or 'étale' embeddings of stable graphs with genus labels. They correspond to restricting a boundary neighbourhood of a stratum of M̄_{g,n} to a sub-curve, as used in modular-operad and graph-category formalisms. The point-subgraph case gives the standard local factors M̄_{g(α), n(α)} of a stratum.
errors: Composition is only asserted, not verified; it does work. Elements of J̃' (half-edges of G' not in G'') map outside f(Ã''). Elements of I' map into I ⊔ J̃, which avoids f(Ã') ⊃ f(Ã''). So the composite lands in I ⊔ J̃'' and stays injective.
In (b) the subscript 'f_{G'}(Ã')' should read f_G(Ã'). In diagram (129), 'I ⊔ A' should be I ⊔ Ã.
Stability of G' (2g−2+n>0 at each vertex) is not imposed, even though non-strict morphisms drop legs. Presumably this is deliberate, or to be handled later.

ideas.what: Half-edge (flag) encoding of dual graphs of stable curves with legs and genus labels
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Trees, 1977) for oriented edges with involution; Kontsevich–Manin 1994 and Getzler–Kapranov 1998 for stable graphs
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower but not this formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Morphisms 'de localisation': subgraph embeddings in which cut half-edges become new legs, preserving genus; strict versus non-strict (forgetting legs); these form a category
ideas.modern_name: subgraph inclusions / étale embeddings of graphs in graphical categories for modular operads; restriction to local factors of boundary strata

ideas.what: Point-subgraph case: the local structure at a vertex α, with legs I_α ⊔ Ã_α
ideas.modern_name: vertex factor M̄_{g(α), n(α)} of a boundary stratum (gluing / clutching maps)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a category of genus-labelled stable graphs with subgraph-localisation morphisms. This is a precursor of the graph categories later used for modular operads, and it predates published versions. It is a historical priority detail rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Un morphisme de localisation de G' dans G est la donnée d'un couple (f_G, f_I) ... Par composition, des ν-graphes et morphismes de localisation [forment une catégorie]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the kind of combinatorial category underlying modular operads and the stratification of M̄_{g,n}. It is of historical interest for Grothendieck's 'structure à l'infini' programme, but mathematically standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine combinatorial definition, a category of subgraph embeddings of stable graphs. It anticipates later formalisms such as Getzler–Kapranov and graph categories for operads, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'simplisme' should read 'morphisme' throughout, and '(de simplification)' likely '(de localisation)', matching the previous page's construction of neighbourhoods of a subgraph.
'Weyl simplisme de simplification' should read 'Un morphisme de localisation'.
'∂_G' should be 'o_G' (the origin map), consistent with o_Ã on the next page.
'f_{G'}(Ã')' should be 'f_G(Ã')'; in diagram (129), 'I ⊔ A' should be 'I ⊔ Ã'.
'ordonné[?]' is uncertain; the struck word before '(f_G, f_I)' is illegible.
The margin note is better read as: 'On dit morphisme de localisation strict si ... I' ≃ (I ⊔ J̃)|S'', i.e. full fibre over S'. The 'S' ≃ S' reading is doubtful.
'Par composition, des ν-graphes et simplismes de simplification' likely continues '... morphismes de localisation [forment une catégorie]'.

The last lines are duplicated in the machine transcription. They read roughly: 'à une notion "orthodoxe" de morphisme de graphes, ou mieux de morphismes de graphes "dans un même sens", par un ν-graphe ...'
